acceptance_criteria.criterion: When `workspace.initialized` is `true`, an "Open in VS Code" button appears in the management row between the Setup button position and the Rename button.
When `workspace.initialized` is `false`, the "Open in VS Code" button is not rendered.
Clicking the button calls `api.workspaces.openVscode(projectId, workspace.id)` and shows a success toast on success.
If the API call fails, an error toast is shown with the error message.
After a successful workspace setup (via the Setup button), the "Open in VS Code" button is dynamically inserted into the management row without a full page re-render.

summary: Added `createOpenVscodeButton(projectId, workspaceId)` helper function in workspace-detail.js that creates the button, wires a click handler calling `api.workspaces.openVscode`, and shows success/error toasts.
In `buildHeaderSection`: when `workspace.initialized === true`, the VS Code button is appended to mgmtRow before the Rename button.

When `workspace.initialized === false`, the Setup button's click handler now dynamically removes itself, creates and inserts the VS Code button via `mgmtRow.insertBefore(vscodeBtn, renameBtn)` after a successful setup — no full page re-render.
Updated module-level JSDoc to document the new 'Open in VS Code' action.
All 27 existing tests pass with no regressions.

comments.note: The `buildHeaderSection` function references `renameBtn` (a `const` declared later in the same function) from within the `setupBtn` click handler closure. This is sound JS — the closure captures the binding, which is fully assigned before any click can occur. However, the forward reference makes the code harder to read at a glance. A minor refactor to hoist `renameBtn` creation before the setup-button block would improve local readability without changing behaviour.

The `createOpenVscodeButton` factory follows the same pattern as other element builders in the file (e.g. `buildRefreshToolbar`, `buildSwitchBranchesButton`). Naming it `build*` instead of `create*` would keep the module's naming convention consistent.

comments.note: Toast calls (success/error) are not directly observable in jsdom without a #toast-container node. The toast module logs '[toast] #toast-container not found' and silently no-ops. AC3/AC4 toast behaviour is therefore validated by inference (button re-enables correctly in both success and error paths via finally block), not by inspecting rendered toast DOM. A browser integration test or a spy on showToast would give stronger toast coverage.
The `createOpenVscodeButton` factory name deviates from the module's `build*` convention (noted by Developer). Not a QA blocker — flagged for code-review attention.

Forward reference to `renameBtn` inside the setupBtn click-handler closure (noted by Developer). Functionally correct; `renameBtn` is always assigned before any user interaction. Minor readability concern — flag for code-review.

comments.note: Renamed `createOpenVscodeButton` → `buildOpenVscodeButton` (JSDoc header, function declaration, and both call sites in buildHeaderSection). The `create*` prefix was inconsistent with the module's established `build*` convention used by buildRefreshToolbar, buildSwitchBranchesButton, buildRenameForm, buildStatusTableSection, etc. This is a pure identifier rename — no behavioral change.

Hoisted `renameBtn` const declaration to the top of the mgmtRow construction block — before the `setupBtn` conditional — and moved its `mgmtRow.appendChild(renameBtn)` call to after the VS Code button conditional. The original code was functionally correct (JS closures capture the binding, not the value, and no click can fire before the function returns), but a reader scanning top-to-bottom would see `renameBtn` used in the setupBtn click handler before its `const` declaration appeared, which is a readability hazard. The hoisted declaration is annotated with an inline comment explaining why it precedes the conditional buttons. DOM insertion order is unchanged: [Setup|VS Code] → Rename → Delete.

Toast side-effects (success/error paths on AC3/AC4) are validated by inference via button state restoration in the finally block. jsdom's lack of a #toast-container means showToast is a silent no-op in tests. For future iterations, consider either (a) injecting a #toast-container div in the test setup and asserting on rendered toast DOM, or (b) adding a module-level showToast spy so toast calls can be asserted directly. Neither gap is a blocker — QA noted this, and the AC acceptance criteria are satisfied.
